workflow: An optimization operation allocates a temporary execution object and inserts it into a long-lived owner.
A conditional handoff does not transfer the operation’s original ownership in one valid path.
The operation returns without releasing that remaining ownership.
Repeated execution leaves each temporary object retained, so leak detection reports persistent memory growth during shutdown.
summary: Successful operation omits cleanup of temporary owned state
decision_reason: The underlying failure is materially the same: a successful operation creates temporary owned state, fails to release an ownership reference on a valid path, and accumulates leaks until shutdown. Implementation-specific execution and runtime terminology has been generalized.
